title: Suffixes and tricky endings
keyIdea: A suffix is an ending added to a root word. -ly makes a how word: sad, sadly. Most roots just add ly, but y after a consonant turns to i (happily), le swaps to ly (gently) and ic adds ally (basically). -ous and -ation start with a vowel, so a final e drops (famous, sensation) and y turns to i (various). The ending that sounds like "shun" has four spellings, and the root's last letters choose: t or te takes -tion (invention), ss or mit takes -ssion (expression, permission), d or se takes -sion (extension, tension), c takes -cian (musician). "zhuh" is -sure (measure), "zhun" is -sion (division) and "chuh" is usually -ture (picture), unless the root ends in ch (teacher). Some words spell a short i with y (myth, gym) or a short u with ou (young, touch).
familyTip: Play root detective in the car or at tea. Say a "shun" word, such as invention, musician or permission, and your child names the root word and its last letters: invent ends in t, so -tion. Then swap: they say a root (act, magic, discuss), you build the word, and they check your spelling by the rule.

visual.caption: Which "shun" spelling does each root take? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: pick the -ly rule, change root letters for -ous and -ation, post roots into four "shun" boxes, match endings to sounds, fill y or ou.

kid: A suffix is an ending you add to a root word. Add ly to sad and you get sadly. Some roots change first. happy turns its y to i: happily. gentle swaps le for ly: gently. basic adds ally: basically.
Some endings start with a vowel, like ous and ation. Then a last e drops. fame becomes famous. sense becomes sensation. vary turns its y to i: various.

The end of a word can sound like shun. Look at the root to spell it. invent ends in t, so we write invention. express ends in ss, so we write expression. extend ends in d: extension. music ends in c: musician. A musician is a person.

Listen to the very end. zhuh is spelt sure, as in measure. chuh is spelt ture, as in picture. teach ends in ch, so it is teacher. Some words just need learning: gym and myth have a y. young and touch have ou.
adult: Ages 7 to 9. The national curriculum for England sets these spellings for Years 3 and 4 (English Appendix 1). They are the suffixes -ly, -ous and -ation. Then come endings that sound like /ʃən/, spelt -tion, -ssion, -sion or -cian. Then /ʒə/ spelt -sure, /tʃə/ spelt -ture and /ʒən/ spelt -sion. Last are y for a short i and ou for a short u. The old rules for vowel suffixes still hold: drop the e, and change y to i.

The -ly rules: most words just add it. After a consonant, y turns to i if the root has two or more beats (happily, angrily). A root that ends in le swaps it for ly (gently, simply). A root that ends in ic adds ally (basically), and publicly is the one common odd word out. For /ʃən/, -tion is the most common spelling, and the root gives the clue. t or te gives -tion, ss or mit gives -ssion, d or se gives -sion, and c gives -cian. attention and intention break the rule. A -cian word is most often a person.

Common mistakes: gentlely and basicly; keeping the e in fameous; writing every /ʃən/ ending as -tion (musition, exprestion); spelling a root plus er as -ture (teature, not teacher); and spelling words the way they sound (mith, yung). The lab gives each slip its own feedback.

In the lab your child picks the -ly rule for eight roots. Next they tap the root letter that changes, or no change, for seven -ous and -ation words. They post twelve roots into the four /ʃən/ boxes by their last letters. They drag -sure, -ture, -sion or -cher into ten gaps from a spoken clue. Last, they fill y or ou into eight words.

practice.prompt: Which way of adding ly to gentle is right?
practice.hint: gentle ends in le. What happens to le before ly?
practice.explain: When a root ends in le, the le swaps to ly: gentle becomes gently. gentlely keeps both, which is a common slip.

practice.prompt: A list has {n} "shun" words. {t} end in -tion and {s} end in -sion. The rest end in -ssion. How many end in -ssion?
practice.hint: Take the -tion and -sion words away from the whole list.
practice.explain: {n} − {t} − {s} = {=n-t-s} words end in -ssion, such as expression and permission.

practice.hint: magic ends in c. Which ending goes with c?
practice.explain: Roots ending in c take -cian: magic, magician. A -cian word is usually a person with a skill.

practice.prompt: Ben spells {a} -ly words and {b} -ous words in a test. How many suffix words does he spell?
practice.hint: Add the -ly words and the -ous words together.
practice.explain: {a} + {b} = {=a+b} suffix words, such as sadly and famous.

practice.prompt: Which word has a short u sound spelt ou?
practice.hint: Say each word. Which one sounds like u in cup but has ou?
practice.explain: touch sounds like tuch but is spelt with ou. cup uses u, and shout has the ow sound.

pool.prompt: Which way of adding ly to basic is right?
pool.hint: basic ends in ic. Words ending in ic add more than ly.
pool.explain: Words ending in ic add ally: basic, basically. publicly is the one common word that breaks this rule.

pool.hint: vary ends in a consonant and y, and -ous starts with a vowel.
pool.explain: Change y to i, then add ous: various. varyous keeps the y and varous drops a letter.

pool.hint: extend ends in d. Which ending goes with d?
pool.explain: Roots ending in d take -sion: extend, extension. Watch out for attention and intention, which break the rule.

pool.prompt: A word sounds like "trezh-uh". How is it spelt?
pool.hint: zhuh at the end is spelt one way.
pool.explain: zhuh at the end is spelt -sure: treasure, measure, pleasure. -ture is for chuh, as in picture.

pool.hint: Is there a root word that ends in ch?
pool.explain: teach is a root word ending in ch, so just add er: teacher. -ture is for words like picture, with no root ending in ch.

pool.prompt: A spelling list has {n} words. {k} of them end in -ture. How many do not?
pool.hint: Take the -ture words away from the whole list.
Roots that end in mit take a double letter ending.
pool.explain: Roots ending in mit take -ssion: permit, permission and admit, admission.

pool.prompt: Each day Maya learns {a} words with y for short i, like gym. How many does she learn in {d} days?
pool.explain: {a} × {d} = {=a*d} words, such as gym, myth and Egypt.

pool.hint: -ous starts with a vowel. What happens to a last e?
pool.explain: The e drops before a vowel ending: famous. The ending is always spelt -ous, never -us.

pool.hint: This word spells its short i sound with a different letter.
pool.explain: myth spells the short i sound with y, like gym and Egypt. These words have to be learnt.
